method: Nine artworks visually inspected by the assistant in this conversation, using their original PNGs, contact sheets, archived metadata and measured stroke/context evidence. These are AI editorial drafts, not human-approved labels or independent model evaluations.

entries.name: nnxyz nifty faces #72
observations: White facial patches and rows of teeth stand against a black field.
Thin red and pale lines repeat around the face, hair and shoulders.
Red marks interrupt the dark eye sockets.
entries.reading: White patches assemble a skull-like face, while red and pale outlines keep its edges unsettled. The teeth are drawn as repeated loops rather than one solid band, making the grin feel insistent. The black ground removes distractions. It can read as confrontational or darkly comic; the image does not fix a single emotion.
entries.contextAngle: This is near the low end of recorded stroke count in Faces, yet its long sampled lines make that count a poor shorthand for visual detail.
entries.connectionReason: Both assemble a toothy, skull-like head from overlapping marks. Compare the restricted red, white and black of Faces #72 with the many-colored overlays and glasses in nnxyz #1.
entries.lookingQuestion: How does the grin change when you look at the teeth as individual loops rather than a single expression?

entries.name: nnxyz nifty faces #113
observations: Dark circular outlines form eyes, a nose and an open circular mouth without an enclosing head outline.
Overlapping pink, peach and pale yellow circles arc above the eyes.
A gray ground occupies much of the image.
entries.reading: A face appears without an enclosing outline: large circular eyes, a small curved nose and a round open mouth are enough to establish it. Overlapping pink, peach and pale yellow circles suggest a loose crown of hair. Their softness plays against the dark arcs below. The expression can suggest surprise, amusement or a moment of puzzled attention.
entries.contextAngle: The short point record and circular forms make a useful counterpoint to the long, unsettled contours in Faces #72. A shared series does not require a shared graphic vocabulary.
entries.connectionReason: Both leave a large open field around a character assembled from rounded shapes. The face in #113 is mostly outlined; the figure in NNOTB #62 is mostly filled.
entries.lookingQuestion: Which few curves make you recognize a face before you notice the colored circles?

entries.name: nnxyz nnotb #1 fork
observations: Several toothy heads overlap with raised limb-like forms.
Yellow, pink, white and blue marks cross the figures and one another.
Broad cyan areas separate parts of the crowded drawing.
entries.reading: Heads and raised, limb-like forms compete for space in a dense weave of colored marks. Teeth recur at different sizes, while broad cyan passages keep small openings between the figures. The drawing alternates between recognizable characters and almost illegible crossings. Looking becomes a process of finding a face, losing it, and finding another.
entries.contextAngle: The title places this beside NNOTB #1, but its archived creation is much later. The number is a title relationship, not evidence that the fork was the next work made.
entries.connectionReason: Both fill the square with competing heads, teeth and crossing lines. Compare the broad cyan gaps here with the tighter black divisions and upright central figure in Rawblocks #0000.
entries.lookingQuestion: Where does a recognizable head dissolve into the surrounding tangle of marks?

entries.name: nnxyz nnotb #62
observations: A small black, rounded, ear-like figure sits toward the lower right.
Yellow lines mark its eyes and stitched-looking grin.
A large yellow square and a broad white frame leave substantial open space.
entries.reading: A small rounded figure sits at the lower right of a broad yellow square. Yellow marks pick out its eyes and stitched-looking grin from the black silhouette. The generous white frame and open field give this modest character unusual presence. Its apparent friendliness is complicated by the fixed smile; the expression remains available to more than one reading.
entries.contextAngle: This sits toward the low end of NNOTB stroke count. Its large open areas provide a useful contrast to the crowded drawing of NNOTB #1 fork, rather than an index of lesser effort.
entries.connectionReason: Both use a framed field and a largely black, rounded figure. NNOTB #62 occupies a small corner; the curved body in Rawblocks #39 fills most of its frame.
entries.lookingQuestion: How much of this figure's character comes from its position in the square rather than its facial marks?

entries.name: nnxyz rawblocks #0000
observations: Several heads and animal-like figures overlap across the square.
A tall, rectangular-headed figure anchors the center.
Black divisions and saturated colored strokes break the drawing into many competing regions.
entries.reading: A tall central figure holds together a crowded field of heads, teeth and smaller animal-like forms. Black divisions cut through bright yellow, turquoise, red and pink passages, so that the eye meets both a framework and repeated interruptions. The square rewards scanning: its surrounding characters resist being reduced to a single central subject.
entries.contextAngle: Despite its zero-padded title, this is a late recorded work among the owned Rawblocks. A numerical starting point would give a different route through the series from an archival timeline.
entries.connectionReason: Both make recognition unstable by crowding several heads and teeth into a crossing field. Their similar abundance offers a bridge between the two named series.
entries.lookingQuestion: Can you follow the central figure without being drawn into the smaller characters at its sides?

entries.name: nnxyz rawblocks #39
observations: A large black figure curves forward, with short projecting marks around its head.
A white eye and a broad white shape within the bent arm interrupt the silhouette.
Olive and yellow-green rectangles form a layered frame.
entries.reading: A black body bends inward against nested olive and yellow-green fields. A white eye and the broad white shape inside the bent arm interrupt its heavy silhouette. The projecting head marks add a prickly edge to an otherwise rounded figure. The pose can suggest absorbed thought or guardedness, but the few facial cues leave its mood unresolved.
entries.contextAngle: This has the smallest recorded stroke count among the owned Rawblocks. That describes the record, not its importance: broad filled forms carry most of the composition.
entries.connectionReason: Both organize a dark rounded figure within a frame, using relatively few recorded strokes. Their very different occupied space makes the comparison more useful than the count alone.
entries.lookingQuestion: What changes if the bent arm reads as a gesture of thought rather than protection?

entries.name: nnxyz #1
observations: A frontal skull-like head has heavy glasses and a wide band of looped teeth.
Many thin colored lines and translucent patches cross the face and its surroundings.
White space remains around parts of the head.
entries.reading: Heavy glasses and a broad band of looped teeth give this frontal head a clear structure. Across it, thin colored lines, pale patches and darker layers repeatedly interrupt that structure. The face feels assembled and revised in view. Its grin can appear theatrical rather than simply cheerful, especially where the glasses obscure the eyes.
entries.contextAngle: This belongs to the separately numbered nnxyz title family, retained outside the three main series. Its repeated teeth and layered face offer a route back to Faces without treating those titles as the same series.
entries.connectionReason: Both build a frontal, toothy head through overlapping colored strokes. Scrimshaw's broad angular marks and open yellow field contrast with the finer crossings and glasses here. This is a formal comparison, not evidence of influence.
entries.lookingQuestion: Do the glasses make this face feel more recognizable, or more like a mask?

entries.name: Scrimshaw 21
observations: A large tilted head stands on an open yellow ground.
Angular multicolored strokes cross the eyes, nose and toothy mouth.
Long black and colored marks fan outward above the head.
entries.reading: A tilted head is built from angular, overlapping marks on a bright yellow ground. The eyes, nose and toothy mouth remain readable even as their contours multiply. Above them, long strokes fan outward and carry the face's restless energy into the surrounding space. The image holds exuberance and strain together rather than settling into a single expression.
entries.contextAngle: The related scrimshaw collection is a separate artist grouping. Its repeated facial contours give a concrete visual basis for the collector's connection with nnxyz, without establishing contact or influence between the artists.
entries.connectionReason: Both use overlapping marks to keep a frontal head recognizable while unsettling its contours. Compare the broad, angular strokes here with the many fine crossings and glasses in nnxyz #1.
entries.lookingQuestion: Which outline of the mouth do you follow first, and how do the other outlines change its expression?

entries.name: Stick Together
observations: Five upright figures stand side by side across the image.
Long colored regions distinguish their bodies while thin lines cross the boundaries.
Looped white and yellow marks hover above the heads.
entries.reading: Five upright figures stand close together, their long colored bodies filling the square. Thin lines cross between them, while differences in facial marks and color keep each figure distinct. Loops above their heads repeat the same gesture across the group. The title invites a reading of solidarity; the uneven faces and tangled boundaries keep that togetherness from feeling uniform.
entries.contextAngle: An unnumbered scrimshaw title is better placed by recorded creation than forced into a numbered sequence. Its group of figures also offers a compositional contrast to the isolated heads in Faces.
entries.connectionReason: Both use repeated contours and tooth-like facial marks, but this five-person group spreads attention across the square while Faces #72 concentrates it on one head. The contrast turns the visitor from individual expression toward a group.
entries.lookingQuestion: Where do the figures remain separate, and where do their lines begin to belong to the group?
